One thing that frustrates me: owners and leaders doing the wrong things at the wrong time, because nobody showed them a better order, or because someone sold them a solution that was unnecessary or out of sequence.
At a networking event last week, someone who connects SMEs with virtual assistants told me about the projects they had on. Rebrands. Website updates. That sort of thing.

Companies get suckered into those by marketers all the time, with no guarantee of more sales or profit, instead of starting with what's actually happening in the business. Yes, the website might be losing traffic or be invisible. But making it look nice and fixing the SEO won't help if the things you changed aren't part of how your buyers find you and decide.

I know an owner who spent a year and a lot of cash putting in an ERP system, when the real problems sat upstream: training, culture, wages, appraisals and the quality management system. Then came the drama. His team put bad material through the shiny new computerised documentation and work planning, and the job had to be done again. They did it deliberately. Their view was "he's making plenty of money but won't give us a pay rise." There were no consequences beyond grumbles, and a private threat that there'd be no bonus or pay rise at the end of the year.

Before you buy the rebrand, the website or the software, ask three questions. What problem is this fixing? Where does that problem actually start? And what has to be true upstream for this to make any difference?
